rollups.text: Crystal Wilson’s pilot project: On 2024-03-10, she reported the script at 40% complete; on 2024-03-15, it was 55%, with a 60% target for 2024-03-22. On 2024-03-15, she endorsed a proposed schedule aiming for a 2024-06-30 delivery within a $120,000 budget, with pre-production March–April, production in May and post-production in June. She focused on script finalization through March and April and planned location scouting for early May; the proposal included weekly check-ins and Trello tracking. On 2024-05-02, she said Trello had improved project tracking by 30% since 2024-04-10. The delivery deadline was later pushed to 2024-07-15 because of casting delays; stakeholders were informed on 2024-04-28. On 2024-07-05, she reported 75% completion, with 12 of 16 scenes filmed and 60% of post-production started. She celebrated 70% filming completion with family at Rendezvous Bay on 2024-07-06. On 2024-09-03, she celebrated 90% overall completion with her team; on 2024-09-05, editing was reported 90% complete, with color grading scheduled for September 10–12. By 2024-11-15, post-production was 95% complete and the final sound mix was scheduled for November 22. On 2024-11-20, she cited the final sound mix due November 22, final cut due December 5, and release planned for December 15; she also stated a goal of 100% post-production by December 5. Elapsed time: 270 days from the first reported script progress (2024-03-10) to the December 5 completion goal; the record does not confirm final completion or release.

Crystal Wilson’s goal to reduce work from 50 hours weekly to 40 by July 2024: she set the goal on 2024-03-15 and planned to assess workload, discuss the goal with her manager, streamline work, delegate, and set boundaries. A proposed timeline placed assessment and manager discussion in April, streamlining and delegation in May, and boundary changes and monitoring in June; she said she would begin with assessment and arranging the meeting. No specific implementation schedule was confirmed. By 2024-07-01, she reported reducing her workweek to 42 hours and reallocating the freed eight hours to family and leisure. On 2024-09-05 and 2024-11-20, she again described her weekly hours as reduced from 50 to 42. Elapsed time: 108 days from goal-setting to the reported 42-hour week; the goal of 40 hours was not reported as achieved.

Crystal Wilson’s stress and mindfulness: On 2024-03-15, she rated stress 6/10, mainly from balancing work and family, and planned mindfulness or meditation, exercise, family activities, and short breaks. In late April, she rated burnout risk 7/10; after starting daily 30-minute mindfulness at 3 PM, stress was 4/10 by 2024-05-01. On 2024-05-02, she said she felt burned out again and wanted to maintain the benefit. She reported stress falling from 6.5 to 4.5 between 2024-08-10 and 2024-09-05, attributing the change to mindfulness. Since 2024-08-15, she had practiced 10-minute breathing exercises at 7:30 AM and said they improved meeting focus. Elapsed time: 174 days from the initial 2024-03-15 stress report to the 2024-09-05 stress update; stress was reported at different scales and circumstances.

Crystal Wilson’s pilot post-production collaboration with Michele: On 2024-04-03, she began weekly Wednesday editing sessions with Michele at 2 PM. By 2024-05-02, she reported footage-review speed had improved 40% and asked how to improve the workflow. On 2024-11-18, she and Michele completed three final-edit scenes in four hours at Montserrat Studios. Separately, on 2024-09-05, Crystal said she had hired Michele as a part-time assistant for 20 hours per week at $25 per hour; assigning her schedule management was only under consideration. Elapsed time: 229 days from the reported start of editing sessions to the November 18 editing session.

Crystal Wilson’s email and call batching: On 2024-03-15, she decided to trial weekly email processing on Fridays from 2–5 PM, with filters and urgent matters routed separately, for four weeks; the intended saving was three hours weekly. From 2024-06-01, she reported batching emails and calls on Mondays and Fridays, saving four hours weekly as of 2024-07-10. Elapsed time: 117 days from the initial trial decision to the reported later time saving; the record does not establish whether the March trial continued uninterrupted.

Crystal Wilson’s recurring exercise, recovery, and rest practices: planned Saturday yoga around 10 AM (undated); began three weekly Pilates classes at Montserrat Wellness Center on 2024-04-22 and later reported more energy; began daily 30-minute mindfulness sessions at 3 PM in late April and reported reduced stress by 2024-05-01; began daily evening meditation at 9 PM on 2024-06-10 and reported sleep rising from six to 7.5 hours; began a no-work-Sundays rule on 2024-06-30, which she said helped reduce stress; began 10-minute morning breathing exercises at 7:30 AM on 2024-08-15 and reported improved meeting focus; maintained a 10 PM bedtime from 2024-08-01 with average sleep of 7.2 hours by 2024-09-05; began 15-minute evening walks on 2024-11-05 and reported improved mood and less screen fatigue; instituted another stated no-work-Sundays policy beginning 2024-11-03 to reduce stress spikes.

Crystal Wilson’s scheduling and task-management tools: Google Calendar synced with a Moleskine planner and weekday two-hour creative blocks beginning at 9 AM (undated); iPhone Reminders for meetings and deadlines, with plans to set 24-hour Google Calendar alerts synced to her iPhone and separate reminder lists (2024-03-15); Trello for pilot-task tracking, which she said improved tracking 30% since 2024-04-10 (reported 2024-05-02); Todoist synced with Google Calendar, which she said increased task completion 25% (reported 2024-05-02); recurring Google Calendar family reminders and a calendar synced with James’s calendar (reported 2024-07-10); integrated Outlook and Google Calendar, with a goal to improve cross-platform scheduling accuracy 15% (after 2024-08-20); Asana automated email reminders were being set up for pilot deadlines (2024-09-05). Trello and Todoist were identified as preferred digital tools on 2024-05-02.

Crystal Wilson’s learning and reading: enrolled in an advanced storytelling online course scheduled to start 2024-04-01, costing $350 (reported 2024-03-15); by 2024-04-20, completed three of six modules and scored 92% on the first quiz; enrolled in a digital-marketing analytics workshop scheduled for 2024-12-01; registered for a digital-marketing webinar for producers scheduled for 2024-07-20, costing $120; by 2024-09-05, was reading Cal Newport’s “Deep Work” and applying its techniques to editing concentration. A separate 2024-09-05 record says she had never read the book and was considering getting it; the records conflict on whether she had started reading it.

Crystal Wilson’s planned or attended social, networking, and creative outings: Alan’s networking event at The Blue Lagoon on 2024-03-22—she decided to attend and planned to contact Alan for details; dinner at The Coral Reef on 2024-04-20 celebrating completion of casting, four guests, $120; charity gala at The Governor’s Mansion on 2024-05-10, invitation from Stephanie and stated intent to attend; Carla’s suggested Emerald Bay Resort retreat on 2024-05-18–19, room booked at $220 per night, but attendance unknown; storyboard work with Alan at The Blue Lagoon café on 2024-06-25, visuals completed in two hours; networking brunch invitation declined on 2024-07-03 to preserve five hours for work; book club at East Janethaven Library on 2024-07-18, invited by Jeffrey, accepted and attendance stated confirmed; Montserrat Botanical Gardens getaway with James planned for 2024-09-14–15 to relax and reconnect; East Janethaven Art Gallery visit with Jeffrey planned for 2024-09-12, but attendance not confirmed; Alan’s dinner invitation declined on 2024-09-02 to protect family dinner time; networking event declined on 2024-11-12 to save five hours for editing; Jeffrey’s East Janethaven Library book launch on 2024-11-28, invitation accepted; creative workshop with Carla at The Blue Lagoon planned for 2024-12-07, with 10 local artists invited, but no attendance or outcome established.

Crystal Wilson’s recorded decisions to decline invitations or offers: declined the March 14, 2024, 3 PM meeting to protect writing time (one meeting); declined a $15,000 documentary contract on 2024-04-15 (one contract; she questioned the decision); declined a networking brunch on 2024-07-03 (one event, preserving five hours); rejected a $25,000 commercial-shoot offer on 2024-08-30 (one offer, prioritizing pilot completion and creative control); declined Alan’s dinner invitation on 2024-09-02 (one invitation, protecting family time); declined a networking event on 2024-11-12 (one event, saving five hours). Total: six recorded declines across meetings, work offers, and social events; not all were social invitations.

Crystal Wilson’s reported time-saving and productivity changes: weekly email batching was intended to save three hours per week (trial decided 2024-03-15); limiting work calls after 7 PM improved evening time with James by two hours weekly (reported 2024-05-02); replacing morning social-media browsing with journaling saved 20 minutes daily from 2024-04-12; batching emails and calls Mondays and Fridays saved four hours weekly from 2024-06-01 (reported 2024-07-10); monthly attendance at Rachel’s school meetings saved three hours monthly (reported 2024-07-10); Sunday meal prep reduced weekday cooking by one hour and takeout costs by $50 weekly (reported 2024-07-10); daily one-hour buffer slots starting 2024-07-01 reduced deadline stress by 35%; rescheduling a client call on 2024-09-01 gave two extra hours; reducing work from 50 to 42 hours weekly freed eight hours. These are distinct reported effects, not a single additive total.

Crystal Wilson’s reported project progress percentages: pilot script 40% on 2024-03-10 and 55% on 2024-03-15; target 60% by 2024-03-22. By 2024-07-05, pilot overall completion was reported at 75%, with 12 of 16 scenes filmed and 60% of post-production started; filming completion reached 70% by 2024-07-06. Editing was reported 90% complete on 2024-09-05, and overall pilot completion reached 90% on 2024-09-03. Post-production was 95% complete on 2024-11-15; a 100% post-production goal was set for 2024-12-05. These percentages describe different stages and are not one continuous measure.

Crystal Wilson’s confirmed project-related spending and budget decisions: endorsed a proposed $120,000 pilot budget on 2024-03-15; dinner celebrating casting at The Coral Reef cost $120 on 2024-04-20; purchased post-production software licenses on 2024-04-25 from a $5,000 allocation (purchase amounts unspecified); said the software-license budget had increased by $6,200 and a sound-editing plugin had been added on 2024-04-28 (plugin price and payment status unspecified); hired Stephanie’s agency for social-media management on 2024-06-20 at $800 monthly; finalized four sound-mixing sessions with Jeremy for 2024-07-12–15 at $150 each, $600 total; registered for a digital-marketing webinar scheduled 2024-07-20 at $120; approved $3,500 for Facebook and Instagram ads and rejected a proposed $5,000 influencer campaign (reported 2024-11-20); pilot-success family celebration planned for 2024-12-20 at The Coral Reef, budget $300 for eight guests. Other figures in proposed sample allocations or illustrative expense examples were not confirmed purchases.

Crystal Wilson’s time with James and family: weekly Friday dinner dates with partner James were planned (undated); a Sunday family movie night at 7 PM was approved (undated); James and Crystal agreed to limit Crystal’s work calls after 7 PM, improving their evening time by two hours per week as reported 2024-05-02; Crystal said on 2024-11-20 she agreed to take no work calls after 6 PM during pilot launch week (dates unspecified); she planned a Montserrat Botanical Gardens getaway with James for 2024-09-14–15 to relax and reconnect; Emma and Michelle began summer camp at East Janethaven Community Center on 2024-06-15, freeing daytime hours; Crystal negotiated monthly rather than more frequent school meetings at Rachel’s school, saving three hours monthly (reported 2024-07-10).
rollups.topic: Family routines and protected family time

rollups.text: Crystal Wilson’s collaborations and mentorship: weekly Monday Zoom call with Laura, an 82-year-old veteran producer (reported 2024-03-15); planned weekly Wednesday 4:30 PM check-ins with Laura about the pilot (time proposed, approval recorded); recurring monthly meetings with Carla, a graphic designer Crystal met at the 2018 Montserrat Film Festival, proposed for the second Saturday, 4–6 PM; met casting director Heather on 2024-03-28 and shifted focus toward casting after Heather recommended early auditions; planned to coordinate a Rendezvous Bay scout and permits with Jeremy for 2024-03-30 to 2024-04-05, although a later 2024-05-02 record says Crystal had never attended a location scout with Jeremy; worked on a storyboard with Alan at The Blue Lagoon café on 2024-06-25 and completed visuals in two hours; co-hosted a 90-minute virtual brainstorming session with Stephanie on 2024-09-03; finalized sound-mixing notes with Jeremy on 2024-09-04 for a September 10 session; met Laura for a review on 2024-11-10, when Laura suggested audience-engagement strategies.

Crystal Wilson’s reported sleep changes: on 2024-03-15, she aimed for seven hours nightly, usually went to bed at 10:30 PM, and said children sometimes disrupted sleep; from 2024-06-10, she practiced evening meditation at 9 PM and reported sleep increasing from six to 7.5 hours; since 2024-08-01, she reported a 10 PM bedtime and average sleep of 7.2 hours as of 2024-09-05. These are dated reports with differing periods and measures, not a single continuous sleep series.
